title: Higher direct image sections vanishing on a principal open are power torsion
statement: Let f : X → T be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], F a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], q a natural number and W an affine open of T. Let M = R^q f_* F [pqf-def-cohomology], a ∈ Γ(T,W), and let r be the restriction from W to the principal open D(a). For every t ∈ Γ(M,W) with r(t)=0, there is n ≥ 0 with a^n t=0.

source.place: Lemma 30.17.3, tensor-unit specialization, combined with Tag 01E4 and the localization criterion for quasi-coherence used in Tag 01XJ (1).

proof.text: Set Y = f⁻¹W, b = f^♯a on Y, and N = H^q(Y,F|Y). The morphism is qcqs and W is affine, so Y is qcqs. Its principal open D(b) is f⁻¹D(a). Restriction preserves quasi-coherence. Here H^q is the right-derived module-section cohomology of RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology, the same theory as the higher-image presheaf; no comparison with abelian-sheaf Ext cohomology is needed.

Apply invertS_cohomology to the tensor unit O_Y, section b, and F|Y. Tensor powers of O_Y identify with O_Y, and tensoring the coefficient module with them is the identity. The canonical fraction relation becomes the ordinary module localization relation. The numerator formula identifies restriction to D(b) with N → N[1/b]; the identification respects scalar multiplication from A = Γ(T,W). Apply this also to every principal open D(c) of W, and its further principal refinements. Explicitly, under the tensor-unit identifications the fraction relations are [n,x]=[n+k,b^k x]. The canonical map sends x/b^n to b^(-n) res(x). This formula proves A-linearity and compatibility with further principal restrictions by checking the fraction generators.

The associated A-module sheaf tilde N has sections N[1/c] on D(c), with the same restriction maps. Thus the cohomology presheaf on the principal-open basis agrees naturally with this sheaf. A sheaf on a basis extends uniquely to the whole space; the sheafification agrees with this extension. The higher-direct-image presheaf theorem identifies that sheafification with R^q f_* F restricted to W, using the same injective section complexes and their cohomology restriction maps. Consequently the actual section restriction on W → D(a) is identified with N → N[1/a], with its scalar action. This reasoning never invokes the Leray affine section comparison, which depends on quasi-coherence.

The section t restricting to zero gives t/1 = 0 in N[1/a]. The zero criterion for localization gives n with a^n t = 0. Transport this identity through the comparison on W. For a=0 the open is empty and one can use exponent 1 for torsion and the zero section for the denominator assertion. Units, degree zero, zero coefficients, and empty W follow from the same localization formulas.
